clue.text: A flat tablet may have this

definitions.text: A flat tablet may have this

parts.note: A flat is a musical key, the one a note above G sharp sits in
a tablet of paper for writing on is a pad

explanation.surface: A remark about touch-screen computers and what they offer for typing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A flat' reads as an adjective on tablet but is a musical key; 'tablet' is a writing pad as well as a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-screen tablet computer shows a set of buttons for entering numbers and letters.

clue.text: Unfinished heroic book is perfect example

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for heroic loses its final letter

parts.note: an epic poem is a heroic one
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A literary critic praising an incomplete heroic work as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the C from EPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that embodies a type perfectly is its quintessence.

clue.text: Takes steps, seeing note added about service

indicators.note: about means the letters of the note wrap around those of the service

parts.note: a note added to a letter is a postscript, PS
an ace is an unreturned service in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone acting after reading a postscript about a tennis serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note added' looks like a musical note but is a postscript added to a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk measured strides, as when one marks out a distance, is to step it out.

clue.text: Missed tea being served? Get a measure of coffee

indicators.note: being served suggests the letters are dished up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who missed out on tea gets a coffee instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being served' rearranges MISSEDTEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup of strong black coffee, served after dinner, takes its name from the French for half-cup.

clue.text: Kind female in front of a church font

indicators.note: in front of places the earlier pieces before the next ones

parts.note: a kind is a type
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A kind woman standing before a church's baptismal font.
explanation.walkthrough: 'font' looks like a church basin but is a set of printing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A font is a printer's design of lettering, such as Times or Arial.

clue.text: People taking exams put up supporters of course

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for put is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to put something down is to set it
tees support balls on a golf course

explanation.surface: Candidates erecting the course's supports, as if setting up hurdles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES; 'course' is a golf course, whose tees hold up the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who sit tests or examinations are examinees.

clue.text: Student's dog seen with girl regularly

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of girl is taken

explanation.surface: A student's puppy is often seen out with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of girl, I and L. The 's of Student's is 'is' and links.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolchild or someone taught by a tutor is a learner of that teacher.

clue.text: Furniture item that pays for plane, perhaps?

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
a plane is a woodworking tool, as the perhaps signals an example

explanation.surface: Wondering which piece of furniture covers the cost of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft but is the carpenter's smoothing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A low stool for resting the feet on is a piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Share drink and consume less

parts.note: one's cut is one's share
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Splitting a drink and so cutting back on alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to reduce one's intake of something, such as sugar or wine.

clue.text: Exciting times crop up on benefit

indicators.note: exciting suggests stirring the letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: Thrilling moments arise for someone living on state benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exciting' rearranges TIMESCROPUPON. Income Support is a British state benefit for people on low income.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British welfare payment to those on low income, a type of state allowance.

clue.text: Number one group gets hearty stew — or a bit of lamb!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a set is a group

indicators.note: hearty means the heart of stew, its middle letters, is used

explanation.surface: A top band is treated to a hearty stew, or perhaps a cut of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearty' takes the middle of stew, TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round boneless piece of lamb loin is a cut of meat.

clue.text: Warning you'll have not so much to do

parts.note: less means not so much
if something is on, there is something to do or happening

explanation.surface: A warning that you will have fewer tasks to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do' is ON as in having a lot on.
explanation.definitionFit: An experience that serves as a caution, as in 'let that be a teaching'.

clue.text: Bristles from challenges

definitions.meaning: confronts boldly, as in to face a lion in its den

explanation.surface: Someone bristling in response to challenges.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names chin hair; the verb means to defy someone face to face.

clue.text: Revolutionary hairstyle that may be held in a net

definitions.text: that may be held in a net

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
a mullet is a hairstyle short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A rebel's haircut that needs a hairnet.
explanation.walkthrough: The net looks like a hairnet for the mullet, but it is a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a prized red sea fish, which fishermen catch in nets.

clue.text: This may be served in a pub — one's ordered

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters are rearranged, as well as drinks asked for

parts.note: the letters of one's are taken as written, O N E S

explanation.surface: Something served in a pub after one orders, like a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges APUBONES. 'served' suggests food or drink, but a writ is served.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ ordering someone to attend court is delivered on them, which is called serving it.

clue.text: Workers protecting women long to make entrances

indicators.note: protecting means the workers surround the other letters

parts.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers
to itch is to long for something

explanation.surface: Staff guard women who long to make grand entrances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' is the verb, to put in a trance, not doors.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to cast a spell over them, enchanting them completely.

clue.text: Virtue in expression of surprise?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether virtue lies in showing surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means moral excellence; it is also an exclamation like 'gracious me!'

clue.text: Rum delivery? That's eccentric

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd
a bowler's delivery in cricket is a ball

explanation.surface: A shipment of rum arriving, labelled as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but means strange; a delivery in cricket is one ball bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun used of an eccentric person: a peculiar, unconventional character.

clue.text: Strike viewer, showing Pacific fish

parts.note: to sock is to punch or strike
the eye is the organ that views

explanation.surface: Punching an onlooker, then displaying a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A red salmon of the North Pacific, prized for canning.

clue.text: Women work after everybody gets beer

indicators.note: after places the work piece behind the everybody piece

parts.note: everybody is all
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Women working after everyone else has got a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for beer or ale, as in a pint of the stuff.

clue.text: Managed part of show as revolutionary turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Displaying someone as a revolutionary who has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Managed part' as the definition, but 'part of' signals the hidden letters, so the definition is 'Managed'. 'turned up' in a down clue reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to supervise or direct a project is to manage it.

clue.text: Smells nothing serious and leaves without permission

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
dour means stern and serious

indicators.note: without means the word for permission is removed from leaves

parts.note: leave is permission, as in leave of absence

explanation.surface: Nothing serious, just someone who goes off without asking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves without permission' looks like going AWOL, but it is leaves minus LEAVE, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: scents or whiffs, things noticed by the nose.

clue.text: Go to court holding for example instruction to proceed

indicators.note: holding means the court word surrounds the example abbreviation

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action in court

explanation.surface: Taking legal action including a sample order to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: In music the word tells the player to go straight on into the next section.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning carry on without a pause into what follows.

clue.text: Company gets at changes in living accommodation

indicators.note: changes means the letters of gets at are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm that criticises changes to housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges GETSAT into TTAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Small country houses are homes, places to live.

clue.text: A win? Encore!

parts.note: to gain something is to win it

explanation.surface: An audience calling for a repeat after a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry from an audience asking a performer for one more.

clue.text: Arguing for a time with lumberjack bosses

parts.note: a logger fells trees
heads are bosses

explanation.surface: Quarrelling for a while with the bosses of a logging firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: in fierce dispute or disagreement with someone.

clue.text: Forestall the rest, keeping alert

indicators.note: keeping says the letters are held within the words before it

explanation.surface: Preempting the others by staying watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span forestALL THE REst.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: mentally sharp, with all one's wits about one.

clue.text: Strength of one fresh on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the ship letters go around the rest

parts.note: a ship's deck is boarded; SS stands for steamship
I is the Roman numeral one
fresh means new

explanation.surface: Where the strength of a new arrival on the team comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention of putting letters inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendons stand for muscular power, as in the sinews of war.
